answer: An agent economy can price every trade by graph distance from trusted seed agents: each hop from the honest core raises the fee, like a river growing colder as it flows from its glacier source toward a distant island. A newcomer near real counterparties pays almost nothing, but a sybil cluster hanging off the graph by a single thin edge sits far from every seed and pays a premium per move. Minting a thousand fakes buys no shortcut closer to the core, because distance is earned through real trade links, not copied keys; the attacker pays a toll per fake while one honest agent trades cheaply.
